E1.evidence: Issue #25 "Keyop core" (maintainer stonier, 2012-04-05): "Fix the launchers to get keyop core functional." closed the next day with "Done." and commit fbe70c7 ("kobuki description started, joint state publisher working, keyop core functional."), whose launch-file diff shows the defective bindings: keyop.launch remapped keyop/cmd_vel to the absolute /robot_core/cmd_vel while base.launch launched the base nodelets inside <group ns="kobuki"> and remapped a non-existent robot_core/control_command to cmd_vel. Maintainer confirmation of a concrete defect; no log.

units_identified: keyop_core (keyop node, external Yujin package; no public repository located)
kobuki_node (KobukiNodelet loaded as robot_core, subscribing to cmd_vel)
E2.evidence: Two units: the keyop_core teleoperation node publishing velocity commands, and the kobuki base nodelet (kobuki_node/KobukiNodelet, nodelet name robot_core) which at the parent revision subscribes to "cmd_vel" on its private handle (kobuki_node.cpp: `velocity_command_subscriber = nh.subscribe(std::string("cmd_vel"), 10, &KobukiNodelet::subscribeVelocityCommand, ...`), i.e. /kobuki/robot_core/cmd_vel under minimal.launch's ns="kobuki". At the parent, keyop.launch (no namespace) had `<remap from="keyop/cmd_vel" to="/robot_core/cmd_vel"/>` and base.launch had `<remap from="robot_core/control_command" to="cmd_vel"/>`, so the teleop published on /robot_core/cmd_vel and nothing was subscribed there. The minimal resolving change binds names only: keyop.launch is wrapped in `<group ns="kobuki">` with `<remap from="keyop/cmd_vel" to="cmd_vel"/>` (and enable/disable likewise), and base.launch changes the remap to `<remap from="robot_core/cmd_vel" to="cmd_vel"/>` (plus a joint_states remap). No declared or referenced interface of either unit changed in the commit: kobuki_node's cmd_vel subscription and message type are untouched, and no keyop_core code is part of the change. Stop at step 3.

E3.evidence: Not reached (the composition would be a PAIR of keyop publisher and base subscriber, but the case is ineligible at E2 step 3).

E4.evidence: Not reached; the source states only that keyop was not functional and is functional after the launch changes.

ineligible_reason: E2 step 3 (deployment_wiring): the teleop and the base were wired to different resolved topic names by their launch files (absolute /robot_core/cmd_vel versus /kobuki/robot_core/cmd_vel, and a stale robot_core/control_command remap); the fix changes only namespaces and remaps.
notes: The commit fbe70c7 is large (kobuki_description package added, joint_states publisher, odometry refactor in kobuki_driver), but the only parts that touch the keyop/base interaction are the two launch files; the teleop node itself (keyop_core, from Yujin's then-external 'ycs' stack, referenced in kobuki_meta/manifest.xml as `<depend package="keyop_core"/>`) is not in this repository and no public copy of its April 2012 source was found, so an interface rename on its side cannot be excluded; the launch diff alone is consistent with wrong bindings. The other nodelet in base.launch, diff_drive_base/DiffDriveBase (mobile_base), also had its cmd_vel remapped to the same namespace-relative name; the base.launch remap source name change (robot_core/control_command -> robot_core/cmd_vel) corrects the remap to the name kobuki_node actually subscribes to rather than reflecting a code change in this commit. The keyop reset_odometry remap was commented out as "Unused". Commit dated 2012-04-06, before the first release tag 0.1.0 (2012-04-20), electric/fuerte era.
